resolution_modes.book_chapter_rule: matched a taxonomy_v1.1 chapter_rule keyed on (book, chapter) — the preferred path, since one chapter title can mean different things in different books
resolution_modes.label_match: no (book, chapter) rule existed, so the normalized chapter label matched a taxonomy entry directly. This is a FALLBACK and is weaker: a bare label match is not book-scoped. A high count here is a prompt to add explicit chapter_rules, not a second endorsed path.
resolution_modes.note: These two counts are a measurement of HOW rows resolved, not a claim that either taxonomy version is short. They sum to taxonomy_resolved.

contracts.verification: answer_provenance / answer_check / derivation_check are three separate signals. derivation_check is 'none' on every row: no pipeline has ever validated a walkthrough. Never collapse these into one 'verified' flag.
contracts.taxonomy: skill_key mirrors the live :Skill name and is the BKT join key; display_label is owner-changeable with zero migration. taxonomy_status 'unresolved' means no id was assigned — the row carries raw_label + normalized_key instead of a fabricated id.
contracts.playability: playable is a verdict; playable_blockers lists why not, so a consumer can widen or narrow the filter without re-deriving it.

known_limits.taxonomy_coverage: question_set records carry NO topic field; the only per-question signal is the book chapter (72% of records). Chapter-derived taxonomy is thin by nature.
known_limits.difficulty_coverage: difficulty is set on ~17% of questions (ETS p_plus and Arun Sharma printed bands); NULL elsewhere because no signal exists. Not imputed.
